analysis.investment_thesis: Eureka Forbes owns the genuinely iconic Aquaguard brand with real pricing power (59% gross margins) and a growing service-AMC network, but at 47x P/E with ROE of only 3.71%, the business is earning far below its cost of capital on a bloated equity base. I don't pay premium prices for businesses that can't yet prove they deserve them.
key_strengths: Aquaguard brand moat in water purification — trusted household name with demonstrated pricing power (59% gross margins)
Debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.02, net cash ~₹5 Cr) with consistent OCF growth: ₹181→194→246 Cr over 3 years
FCF generation improving (₹190 Cr in FY25) and capital intensity is low (capex only ₹60 Cr vs OCF ₹246 Cr)
key_risks: ROE of 3.71% and ROCE of 5.07% are catastrophically below my 15% threshold — the business earns less than a fixed deposit on its equity base
Valuation is demanding at 47x P/E and 32x EV/EBITDA with FCF yield under 2% (₹190 Cr FCF / ₹9,319 Cr market cap)
PE-backed promoter (Lunolux/Advent International at 62.56%) creates exit overhang risk — PE firms sell, not hold forever
red_flags: ROE of 3.71% on equity of ₹4,520 Cr suggests the demerger/listing created a massively goodwill-inflated equity base that destroys apparent returns
Operating margin of only 7.97% despite 59% gross margins signals heavy distribution/service costs eating the brand's pricing power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Eureka Forbes is a recognizable consumer brand with a genuine moat in water purification — Aquaguard is a verb in many Indian households, much like Xerox or Band-Aid in America. The 59% gross margin confirms real pricing power exists, and the AMC (Annual Maintenance Contract) service network creates switching costs. Revenue has grown from ₹2,085 Cr to ₹2,437 Cr (FY23-FY25, ~8% CAGR on an organic basis), and FCF has steadily improved to ₹190 Cr in FY25. The balance sheet is clean with D/E of 0.02. These are the bones of a decent business.

However, the ROE of 3.71% disqualifies this from serious consideration at my desk. The equity base of ₹4,520 Cr is massively inflated from the 2022 demerger/listing, but even adjusting for that, operating margins of 8% on ₹2,437 Cr of revenue suggest the distribution-heavy direct sales model consumes most of the brand's value. I'm being asked to pay 47x earnings for a business yielding under 2% on FCF with a PE firm as the controlling shareholder — that's a combination that makes me reach for the reject stamp. The business may improve as scale builds and margins expand, but at this price, there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
